question: Should the 3.9.6 release permit CLI-only upgrades to leave pre-3.8 Bridge hosts unable to authenticate, or must the release preflight, block, or guide that upgrade?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes a signed-client compatibility contract; selecting an acceptable upgrade policy is a release-owner decision, not a mechanical review correction.

options.title: Add a compatibility preflight
options.body: Detect an incompatible pre-3.8 Bridge host before using the newly signed CLI and present a direct upgrade or recovery action, with focused validation for legacy and supported hosts.

options.title: Accept the documented compatibility floor
options.body: Release with the stated 3.8+ host requirement and explicitly own the CLI-only upgrade break as a supported migration constraint.

options.title: Defer the CLI signer migration
options.body: Keep the transition-era CLI signer until an upgrade-safe host migration path is available.

recommendation.title: Add a compatibility preflight
recommendation.body: Detect an incompatible pre-3.8 Bridge host before using the newly signed CLI and present a direct upgrade or recovery action, with focused validation for legacy and supported hosts.

likelyOwner.reason: The collaborator authored the release migration and is the clearest available routing candidate for the signing and release compatibility decision.
